title: RWT-S16: linear samples with a retained threshold witness

claims.statement: For RWT-S16 of proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), k=2(n+16), h=floor(k/16), and r=floor(3 sqrt(2^n)/4) on the N>=3 branch, under both the clean source and the adversarial good-marginal model in claim 4 with epsilon(n)=1/16, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 95/128>2/3. Worst-case total charged sequential work is O(2^(n/2) n^2 (log2(n+2))^2), including all classical bit operations, generation, addressing, source acquisition and every branch. The full asymptotic representative is B_T(n)=2^(n/2)n^2(log2 n)^2 for n>=2, with B_T(1)=1; its exact growth index is 1. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with claims 1-4.

For RWT-S16 of proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), k=2(n+16), h=floor(k/16), and r=floor(3 sqrt(2^n)/4) on the N>=3 branch, under both the clean source and the adversarial good-marginal model in claim 4 with epsilon(n)=1/16, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 95/128>2/3. Worst-case peak classical allocation is O(n) bits, including the input, parameters, integer scratch, loop counters and streamed gate descriptor. The full representative B_C(n)=n has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with claims 0,2,3,4.

For RWT-S16 of proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), k=2(n+16), h=floor(k/16), and r=floor(3 sqrt(2^n)/4) on the N>=3 branch, under both the clean source and the adversarial good-marginal model in claim 4 with epsilon(n)=1/16, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 95/128>2/3. Worst-case peak quantum allocation is O(n^2) qubits, including all k(n+1) retained source qubits, candidate, counters, flags and reusable arithmetic scratch. The full representative B_Q(n)=n^2 has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with claims 0,1,3,4.

For RWT-S16 of proof.md, for every integer N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), k=2(n+16), h=floor(k/16), and r=floor(3 sqrt(2^n)/4) on the N>=3 branch, under both the clean source and the adversarial good-marginal model in claim 4 with epsilon(n)=1/16, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 95/128>2/3. Every execution branch acquires exactly Q=2(n+16) source copies, once each, hence O(n). This includes all acquired copies on wrong-answer branches; there are no extra or restarted acquisitions. The full asymptotic representative B_samples(n)=n has exact growth index 0. All constants are absolute. This holds jointly with claims 0,1,2,4.

For the same RWT-S16 configuration in proof.md, for every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ with n=ceil(log2 N), the guaranteed malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=1/16 among exactly Q=2(n+16) copies acquired before testing. At most floor(Q/16) positions may be malformed. An adversary fixes their set, possibly depending on N,s; the joint state is arbitrary provided its reduced state on all remaining positions is exactly rho_s^{tensor (Q-|B|)}. Malformed registers have the same dimensions and may be correlated or entangled subject to that marginal promise; there is no later replacement or access to B, source control, purification or inverse preparation. Under every such state (including the clean source), full-secret recovery has unconditional probability at least 95/128>2/3 jointly with all four worst-case resource bounds. This fraction is a guaranteed tolerance, not a maximum or a per-copy stochastic error probability.

structured.error_model: Among the Q acquired copies, an adversary fixes a set B of at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) malformed positions, possibly depending on N and s. The joint state is arbitrary subject to its reduced state on all other positions being exactly rho_s^{tensor (Q-|B|)}. Malformed systems may be correlated or entangled with each other and with other systems subject to that marginal promise. No source control, purification access, or preparation inverse is supplied.
